title: The Krauken Fermentation Profile Library
description: Complete fermentation workflows for major yeast strains
how_to_use: 1. User selects a yeast from the Krauken yeast database
2. Controller looks up yeast_code in this profile library
3. Display recommended_workflow as a stage-by-stage timeline
4. At each stage, hold temperature and wait for completion_criteria
5. Once complete, advance to next stage

stage_descriptions.PRIMARY: Main fermentation, 80-90% sugar consumed (5-14 days typical)
stage_descriptions.FREE_RISE: Optional: stop cooling, let temp rise from yeast heat (2-7 days)
stage_descriptions.DIACETYL_REST: Optional (mandatory for lagers): raise temp to clean buttery flavor (2-6 days)
stage_descriptions.CONDITIONING: Optional (mandatory for lagers): cold storage for flavor maturation (0-56 days)
stage_descriptions.COLD_CRASH: Optional: rapid chill to clarify via yeast flocculation (24-48h)
stage_descriptions.BOTTLE_COND: Secondary fermentation in sealed bottles for carbonation & maturation (21-84+ days)

primary_fermentation.monitoring: gravity check every 2-3 days after day 2

free_rise.reason: Clean American ale; free rise would add unwanted esters

diacetyl_rest.reason: Low diacetyl production strain; fermented warm naturally cleans diacetyl
diacetyl_rest.note: White Labs FAQ still recommends 48h @ 62-70°F after reaching FG if desired

conditioning.reason: Not required; American ales can go straight to cold crash

primary_fermentation.monitoring: gravity check every 2-3 days after day 3
primary_fermentation.note: Cold fermentation is intentional; slow and clean

diacetyl_rest.timing: Begin when 2-5 points above target FG (approx day 10-12)
procedure: Raise temperature 2-3°F per day over 1-2 days (don't shock)
Hold at 65°F for 2-3 days
Gravity should reach terminal by end of diacetyl rest
diacetyl_rest.critical: Must do in PRIMARY (yeast in suspension); don't rack before

procedure: After diacetyl rest, gradually cool 2-3°F per day to 40°F
Hold at 40°F for 4-6 weeks (traditional lagering)
Longer lagering = cleaner, more refined flavor
conditioning.purpose: Flavor maturation, yeast settling, off-flavor cleanup

cold_crash.purpose: Final clarity polish; settles remaining yeast/proteins

procedure: Days 1-3: Room temp (68-72°F) to carbonate
Days 4-21: Cold storage (fridge, 40°F) to mature

recommended_workflow: Day 12-15: DIACETYL REST: raise to 65°F over 2 days, hold 2-3 days
Day 15-60: CONDITIONING: gradually cool to 40°F, hold 4-6 weeks
Day 78: READY TO DRINK (longer aging OK, even recommended)
WLP800.note: Traditional lager brewing takes 10-12 weeks; worth it for clean, refined beer

WLP590.yeast_name: White Labs French Saison Ale Yeast

primary_fermentation.note: Saisons are slow and unpredictable; extended fermentation normal

free_rise.timing: After 5-7 days at 68°F (after lag + early growth phase)
free_rise.method: Stop active cooling; let yeast metabolic heat warm naturally
free_rise.purpose: Enhance pear, apple, spice esters; promote attenuation
free_rise.risk: If above 80°F, may produce unwanted fusel/heat stress flavors

diacetyl_rest.optional: If you detect butter/VDK, hold warm for 1-2 extra days

conditioning.reason: Belgian ales go to bottle conditioning for flavor development

cold_crash.reason: Saisons benefit from continued slow fermentation; no cold crash

procedure: Days 1-21: Room temp (68-72°F) for carbonation + continued fermentation
Days 22-84+: Cold storage or room temp (flavor develops either way)
Wait 2-3 months before first tasting
bottle_conditioning.note: Saisons improve dramatically with 3-12 months aging

recommended_workflow: Day 8-21: FREE RISE: stop cooling, let temp rise to 75°F over 2 days, ferment 3-5 days
Day 21-42: FINISH PRIMARY: let temp fall back, complete attenuation
Day 42-63: BOTTLE CONDITION @ 70°F (3 weeks carbonation + continued fermentation)
Day 63+: CONDITION: can keep at room temp or cold storage
Day 84: TRY FIRST BOTTLE (but really, wait 3-6 months)
WLP590.note: Saisons are a commitment; patience is rewarded with complex flavor

primary_fermentation.monitoring: gravity check every 2-3 days after day 2
primary_fermentation.note: Pitch rate affects banana:clove ratio; underpitch slightly for more banana

free_rise.method: Reduce active cooling; let natural heat rise temp 2-3°F
free_rise.purpose: Enhance banana (isoamyl acetate) and clove (phenolic) esters
free_rise.note: This is where the classic hefeweizen character comes from

conditioning.reason: Wheat beers drink fresh; can go straight to cold storage

cold_crash.reason: Haze is a feature of hefeweizen; cold crash would remove it
cold_crash.note: You WANT yeast in suspension; serve with yeast

procedure: Days 1-3: Room temp (68-72°F) for carbonation
Days 4-21: Cold storage or room temp (drink fresh)

recommended_workflow: Day 5-7: FREE RISE: let temp rise to 72°F, ferment 2-3 days
WLP300.note: Hefeweizens are fast and fun; enjoy fresh

S-23.beer_style: Hoppy Lager, Fruity Lager, Dry Lager

primary_fermentation.monitoring: gravity check every 2-3 days after day 3
primary_fermentation.note: S-23 is highly attenuative (80-90%); expect low FG

procedure: Gradually raise temp 2-3°F per day to 65°F
Hold for 2-3 days minimum
Beer should reach final gravity during this rest
After diacetyl rest, cool slowly to 40°F
Hold for 3-4 weeks minimum
S-23's fruity notes develop during lagering
Days 1-3: Room temp to carbonate
Days 4-21: Cold storage

recommended_workflow: Day 2-10: PRIMARY @ 50°F (highly attenuative; reaches ~80% FG early)
Day 10-12: DIACETYL REST: raise to 65°F, hold 2-3 days
Day 12-40: CONDITIONING: cool to 40°F, hold 4 weeks
S-23.note: S-23 is excellent for fruity/hoppy lagers; the dry finish makes hops pop
